newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Raytheon to start implementing Brazil Sivam deal.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon to start implementing Brazil Sivam deal.

text.p: U.S. defense giant Raytheon Co has announced that financing for the $1.285 billion Amazon Vigilance System (Sivam) has been authorized, which allows Raytheon to start implementing the program.

As part of Brazil's plan to improve surveillance of its vast and largely unchartered Amazon region, Raytheon will provide and install air traffic control radars, environmental monitors, meteorological radars and other equipment.

Financing for the controversial vigilance system, which was held up for more than two years amid political wrangling and concerns over its cost, will come from four sources: The U.S. Eximbank, Sweden's export bank AB Svensk Exportkredit, Raytheon and Sivam Vendor Trust.
Raytheon said the U.S. Eximbank will provide most of the financing with loans of more than $1 billion.
Sivam is due to be fully operational within five years and should help Brazil protect the rainforest, improve air safety and border control, and better plan land use.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
